country: France, other European countries, United States/Canada, South America (multinational)

links.outcome: iBox discrimination and calibration across external validation cohorts from different sites
links.effect: C index 0.79-0.87 and Brier 0.08-0.11 across cohorts; calibration adequate in some but not all external cohorts, with over- or underestimation of risk.
links.quote: Calibration was adequate in some but not all external validation cohorts, with trends toward overestimation or underestimation of predicted risks.

links.outcome: Predictive ability of iBox versus eGFR slope and anti-HLA donor specific antibodies
links.effect: iBox C index 0.81 vs eGFR slope 0.62 and vs donor specific antibodies 0.57.
links.quote: The iBox was also superior to eGFR slope (C index 0.81 v 0.62) and circulating anti-HLA donor specific antibodies (C index 0.81 v 0.57) in its predictive ability.

links.outcome: iBox performance when extended to new clinical contexts and longer prediction horizon
links.effect: C index 0.81 with race-free eGFR equations; 0.74-0.87 across recurrence, BK virus, and immunosuppressive strategies; 0.79 at 10 years.
links.quote: The model performed well with different race-free eGFR equations (C index 0.81), in various clinical scenarios, including disease recurrence and BK virus nephropathy, with different immunosuppressive strategies, such as calcineurin inhibitors and mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) inhibitors (C index range 0.74-0.87), and when extending the prediction period to 10 years after risk evaluation (C index 0.79).

unlisted_practices: Evaluating a prediction model with competing-risk-of-death analysis and decision curve analysis for clinical utility

screen.reason: The study conducts comprehensive international external validation and clinical scenario testing (including race-free equations and subgroup evaluations) of the iBox risk prediction system for kidney allograft failure.
